title: Scene 6's payoff card is already fully on screen in scene 3
detail: Scene 3's frame contains the entire 'Children treated — the figure, and the measurement' card: 48,787 courses delivered, 99 / 122 recorded recoveries, 81.1% observed recovery rate, all three explanatory captions, and the first row of the discharge table. Scene 6 shows the same card. The only genuinely new pixels in the finale are three more discharge rows (Defaulted 17, Transferred to inpatient care 3, Non-response 3) and the Sphere-thresholds footnote. Scene 6's narration frames it as a reveal — 'Beside it now sits a different figure' — but the viewer met that figure three scenes earlier, in the frame that was supposed to be about cost-per-child method.
fix: Change scene 3's second scroll_to so the viewport stops at the method note and does NOT include the Children-treated card. Scene 3's content is the ladder and the method; the payoff card is not its content. This is the single highest-leverage edit in the run and it is a one-line recipe change.

title: The most striking artifact arrives second and is never topped
detail: The sankey in scene 2 is the run's visual peak. Scenes 3 and 6 are stat cards and tables; scene 5 is horizontal bars and a two-row coverage table. The finale is conceptually the strongest argument in the narrative but visually the flattest frame in the sequence — and it is a frame the viewer has already substantially seen. The intellectual arc rises while the visual arc falls.
fix: Either give the finale a visual it owns (the promised batch-to-child MUAC drill — see arc-07), or move the sankey later so the run does not spend its best picture in position two.

title: Scene 3's removal would not be noticed
detail: Scene 3's unique content is the four-step ladder ($2.4M → 1,589 MT → 115,170 cartons → 115,170 children) and the method note beneath it. Both reappear verbatim and in full at the top of scene 6's frame. If scene 3 were cut, scene 6 would still show everything scene 3 showed, and nothing else in the run depends on scene 3 having happened. Rubric rule 'any scene whose removal would not be noticed: max 3' and 'two scenes showing the same surface with only a scroll between them: max 2' both fire on this pair.
fix: Same edit as arc-01 solves both: tighten scene 3's viewport to the ladder + method note, and start scene 6's viewport BELOW the ladder so the two frames share nothing. If that is not possible, cut scene 3 and fold its method beat into scene 1 or 6.

title: Three consecutive scenes each leak the next scene's subject into their own frame
detail: Scene 1's frame opens on the bottom node of the sankey ('FY2026 Famine Prevention …') and the sankey's own reconciliation caption, which is scene 2's subject; scene 2 then presents the sankey as new. Scene 1 also already shows the top of the 'What a dollar bought' ladder, which is scene 3's subject. Every reveal in the opening three scenes is pre-announced by the frame before it.
fix: Retune the scroll offsets so each of scenes 1, 2, 3 lands on a viewport containing its own card and no part of the next one. The cards are tall enough that this is achievable at 1280x720.

title: Four of six scenes are the funder page at four scroll offsets
detail: Surface A (funder view) carries scenes 1, 2, 3 and 6 — four scroll positions of one page, with 1 and 2 overlapping on the sankey and 3 and 6 overlapping on the ladder, the method note and the payoff card. Surface B (Nigeria government view) carries scenes 4 and 5, which are genuinely non-overlapping and are the healthiest pair in the run. Rubric rule 'more than half the scenes are the same surface at different scroll offsets: max 2' fires.
route_rationale: Routed CONCEPT, not PRODUCT. The product does NOT have only one surface to show — it renders a sankey, three-stage progress bars per contract, a four-step KPI ladder, side-by-side comparison cards, a horizontal stock bar chart and an IPC-tagged coverage table. The narrative simply chose to revisit the same page four times. No new chart types need building.
fix: Sequencing and framing, not product work. Give each funder-view scene a viewport whose content appears in no other frame, and consider whether the six beats need six scenes — five tight frames over the same two surfaces would look more varied than six overlapping ones.

title: The scene-4 hand-off is motivated on screen; the scene-6 hand-back is not
detail: Scene 4 is a model transition: the header chip changes from Funder to Government observer, 'Dale Whitmore' becomes 'Hauwa Ibrahim', the page title becomes 'Nigeria — supply overview', and the sidebar collapses to a single 'Country overview' item. The switch is visible, not merely asserted. Scene 6 is the opposite: the chip flips silently back to Funder / Dale Whitmore and the narration opens 'Here is the number every report leads with' with no acknowledgement that we have left Hauwa's screen. The recipe's `show` field says 'Back on the funder view' but the locked narration does not, and narration is what the viewer hears.
fix: Add a clause to scene 6's narration that motivates the return — something that carries Hauwa's coverage finding back to Dale as the reason he is looking again (her uncovered-children figure is, by the narrative's own words in scene 5, 'the same figure that justifies the next appropriation'). That sentence exists in scene 5 and is the natural bridge; it is currently doing no work.

title: The finale's most vivid promise has no on-screen referent
detail: Scene 6's narration promises that 'Dale can follow a single delivered batch through the distributions it fed to one child's arm circumference climbing out of the red', and the recipe's feature list declares a batch-to-outcome drill (batch-to-outcome-drill, DistributionRecord → ChildOutcome measurement series). Nothing of the sort is in the frame: no batch drill-in, no per-child view, no MUAC series, no time chart anywhere. The screen shows a static three-card summary and a four-row aggregate discharge table. The single most concrete image in the whole narration — the one thing that makes this a story about a child rather than a story about arithmetic — is not rendered.
verified: The drill EXISTS as an API only. connect_labs/supply/urls.py:80 routes api/batches/<batch_lot>/ to demand_api.batch_drill, and connect_labs/supply/tests/test_demand.py:655 asserts it returns records + outcomes with latest_muac_mm crossing MUAC_RECOVERED_MIN_MM. There is no front-end that renders it: grepping the supply app and the repo's JS for 'muac' or 'api/batches' finds zero UI references outside docs/workflows/single_client_weight_trend.jsx, which belongs to the workflow engine, not the supply site. So the narration is describing a payload, not a screen.
fix: Two options. (a) Cheap and honest: cut the MUAC clause from scene 6's narration — but that removes the run's only human image and leaves the finale visually flat (see arc-02). (b) Expensive and correct: build the batch-drill panel on the funder view against the endpoint that already exists and is already tested, and give scene 6 a click action into it. Option (b) is the only one that also fixes arc-02 and arc-05, because it is the one new surface the run needs.
cost: expensive — API and tests exist, the UI does not

title: The run opens on the bottom of a chart and closes on an empty heading
detail: Scene 1's spec says it shows 'obligated, disbursed and delivered as three separate figures in the key row'. The key-figures row is cut off ABOVE the viewport — only its tail appears, in scene 2. The first thing the viewer sees is the bottom half of a sankey node they have no context for. At the other end, scene 6's final frame terminates on the section heading 'Coverage against need, by country' with nothing beneath it: the last thing the viewer sees is the title of a section that never renders.
fix: Scene 1: drop the scroll_to, or scroll to a position that includes the .keyfigures row — the narration is about those three figures and they should be on screen while it says so. Scene 6: end the hold on the discharge table's Sphere footnote rather than letting the viewport run past it into the next heading.

title: Three different 'children' numbers across the sequence with no on-screen bridge
detail: 115,170 'Children treated' appears in the funder key row and the ladder (scenes 1, 3, 6); 43,782 'Children treated' appears in Hauwa's key row (scene 4); 48,787 'Courses delivered' appears in the payoff card (scenes 3, 6). Global-versus-Nigeria scoping explains the first pair and the finale's entire point is that the last two mean different things — but a viewer moving 3 → 4 → 6 watches the same headline noun change value twice with nothing on screen or in narration marking the change of denominator. Only a sequence judge can see this; each scene is individually defensible. There is also a mild self-undercut: the funder key row still headlines '115,170 Children treated' as a single figure, which is exactly the collapse scene 6 spends its narration attacking.
fix: One clause at the scene-4 boundary naming the scope change, and consider whether the funder key row's 'Children treated' tile should be relabelled 'Courses delivered' so the top of the page does not commit the sin the bottom of the page indicts.
